prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: asking to pay a premium monthly instead. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member asks to pay the premium monthly instead, I check whether the policy can stay in force and whether the change affects any outstanding claim handling before I suggest the next step."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a change to monthly instalments is requested mid-claim, I make sure any arrears, missed payments or collection issues are identified first, because payment status can affect cover and delegated authority decisions."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member is anxious about upfront cost, I prefer to explain the monthly option in plain language and keep the focus on what happens next, rather than on the full annual premium at once."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a claim is already open, I do not assume monthly payments are automatically available; I verify the policy terms and any underwriting conditions before confirming anything."},{"type":"fact","content":"When I see a preference for monthly payments, I check whether the instalment plan includes any administration charge or interest so the member can make an informed choice."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member wants to switch to monthly because of an unexpected bill, I treat it as a budgeting request and avoid linking it to the claim outcome, which keeps the conversation calmer."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is urgency, I prefer to tell the member exactly what I can change now and what needs separate approval, rather than leaving monthly payment options vague."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the policyholder is near renewal, I check whether it is better to set monthly payments at renewal rather than amend the current term, as that is often simpler and less error-prone."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the insured has both home and motor cover, I review each policy separately before discussing monthly payment plans, because one policy may be eligible and the other may not be."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I record the request, I write down that the member asked to pay monthly instead and the reason given, so the next handler can see the context without repeating the same questions."}]}
